newsitem.title: USA: D'Amato opposes new Whitewater hearings.
newsitem.headline: D'Amato opposes new Whitewater hearings.

text.p: Sen. Alfonse D'Amato, who chaired 60 days of tumultuous hearings by a special Whitewater committee, said on Wednesday Congress should now forget about further investigations of President Bill Clinton.

"It seems to me we should leave that in the hands of the special prosecutor and not be attempting to substitute our judgment," the New York Republican said at a news conference, speaking of Whitewater and the election.

D'Amato, an influential Republican who chairs the Banking Committee, led the fight for hearings on Whitewater last year and pushed relentlessly to link Clinton to wrongdoing. The committee concluded with a report highly critical of the president and his wife, Hillary Rodham Clinton.

But D'Amato turned over a new leaf at his news conference, saying he saw no need for further congressional investigations into Whitewater or possibile irregularities in Democratic campaign fundraising.
"Our job is to work in common toward the goals that the president has articulated during the campaign, many of which are goals that Republicans have been fighting for," D'Amato said.
He said Republican Congress and the Democratic president must work together to balance the budget, repair financial problems with Medicare and make the transition workable from welfare to jobs.

Pressed about his views, D'Amato said: "I think I understand a little bit about holding hearings, but everyone has to make his or her decision ... there are appropriate authorities" to look into any wrongdoing.
